newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 31.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:
* General Motors's $500 million deal to sponsor five consecutive Olympics on NBC is the first of its kind, but it won't be the last.
* Sony's Columbia Pictures is in final talks with Yoko Ono on a deal to develop a feature film about her romance with John Lennon.
* General Electric's NBC and Fox's Twentieth TV are in talks to dissolve the syndie programming partnership News Corp inherited last year with its purchase of New World Communications.
* A bitter battle is being fought between rival camps attempting to bring some formal organization to this year's pre-Mifed film screenings in London.

* MGM has officially re-entered the network TV business after a three-year absence with CBS' midseason order for the drama "The Magnificent Seven," which is expected to be announced Thursday. Westinghouse CBS has also picked up "Unsolved Mysteries," which NBC canceled after nine seasons.

* Twentieth Century Fox TV has signed a three-year overall development deal with veteran writer-producer John Tinker and director-producer Bill D'Elia, executive producers of the CBS drama Chicago Hope.
